items.statement: C–C bond formation and trans lactone ring closure of the acid substrate
items.expected: Actual molecular structures and reaction-connectivity evidence support C–C bond formation between the specified E-hex-3-enoic acid and an adamantyl electrophilic center, and ring closure through carboxyl oxygen to the supplied five-membered lactone with a trans ethyl/adamantyl relative configuration. The authors' reference is a concerted cyclization TS retaining the acidic proton, with total charge +1 and singlet multiplicity. The reaction mode and local connectivity must correspond to these bond-forming events, and the protonated endpoint must be related to the neutral target product with balanced atoms/protons. Scientifically equivalent connectivity evidence is permitted; a full IRC or deprotonation TS is not mandatory. The supplied product, one correct distance or normal termination alone is insufficient.

items.statement: C–C bond formation and trans nitrogen-containing ring closure of the sulfonamide substrate
items.expected: Actual structures and local reaction connectivity support C–C bond formation and five-membered N–C ring closure of the complete specified E-alkenyl sulfonamide, giving the trans ethyl/adamantyl relationship in the supplied N-p-toluenesulfonylpyrrolidine. The authors' TS retains the N–H proton, with total charge +1 and singlet multiplicity; the protonated endpoint must be reasonably related to the neutral product. An unconverged supermolecule cannot be presented as a minimum, but valid reaction modes, finite downhill paths and independently qualified fragments may provide commensurate evidence. A complete catalytic cycle or cis competition is not required.

items.statement: Local cyclization Gibbs barrier of the acid substrate
items.expected: G(TS1–3a)−G(Ad+)−G(1a)=13.0 kcal/mol, with absolute tolerance 2.0 and inclusive boundaries. Check HFIP, 293.15 K, 1 atm, +1 singlet reacting components and retention of the acidic proton. The TS must have saddle-point/connectivity evidence corresponding to the bond formation. This quantity is not the 15.7 height on the full profile starting from AdOH; do not splice the authors' ionic energy of 2.7 into independently computed local quantities. Reconstruction of solvent thermal corrections must be explicit. Physically equivalent standard-state/unit conversions are permitted; fitted offsets are not accepted.

items.statement: Local cyclization Gibbs barrier of the sulfonamide substrate
items.expected: G(TS1–3s)−G(Ad+)−G(1s)=10.2 kcal/mol, with absolute tolerance 2.0 and inclusive boundaries. Check HFIP, 293.15 K, 1 atm, the complete E-sulfonamide and a +1 singlet TS retaining the N–H proton, with actual saddle-point/connectivity evidence. This quantity is not the 12.9 height on the full profile starting from AdOH. All energies must come from a consistent independently computed ledger; do not mix the authors' ion-formation energy with independently computed local energies. Transparent, physically equivalent conversions are permitted.

items.statement: Net Gibbs free energy of lactone formation
items.expected: G(trans lactone 3a)+G(H2O)−G(AdOH)−G(E-alkenyl acid 1a)=−12.3 kcal/mol, with absolute tolerance 2.0 and inclusive boundaries. Use valid neutral singlet minima and consistent thermal corrections for HFIP, 293.15 K and 1 atm; TfOH/HFIP cancel as conserved spectator components in the complete ledger. A protonated product, ion-pair energy or arbitrary lower conformer cannot replace this net reaction quantity without an explicit identity account.

items.statement: Net Gibbs free energy of nitrogen-containing cyclic product formation
items.expected: G(trans N-p-toluenesulfonylpyrrolidine 3s)+G(H2O)−G(AdOH)−G(E-alkenyl sulfonamide 1s)=−12.1 kcal/mol, with absolute tolerance 2.0 and inclusive boundaries. Use valid neutral singlet minima for HFIP, 293.15 K and 1 atm; retain the complete substrate, atom and proton ledger. A cationic endpoint retaining an extra N–H cannot directly replace the neutral net product.
